title: Brand Identity Design
shortDescription: Complete visual identity system for a luxury boutique brand.
fullDescription: This project involved designing a complete visual identity system from the ground up for a high-end luxury boutique brand. Starting from a brand discovery phase — understanding the target audience, tone, values, and competitors — I developed a cohesive system that includes a primary logo, logo variations, a refined color palette, custom typography pairing, business card design, packaging mockups, and a full brand guidelines document. Every element was crafted to communicate elegance, exclusivity, and timeless sophistication.
features: Primary logo with three approved variations (horizontal, stacked, icon-only)
Custom color palette with precise CMYK, RGB, and HEX codes for print and digital use
Typography system using a serif headline font paired with a clean sans-serif body font
Full stationery set: business card, letterhead, envelope, and email signature
Packaging design for product boxes, tissue paper, and shopping bags
50-page brand guidelines PDF documenting all rules and usage examples
challenges: The client had a very specific vision but found it difficult to articulate. I solved this by running a structured visual preference exercise — presenting mood boards, competitor analysis, and style references — which allowed the client to express preferences visually rather than verbally. This became the creative foundation for every decision that followed.
outcome: The brand launched successfully and the client reported a significant increase in perceived brand value from their customers. The identity has been consistently applied across all touchpoints — both physical and digital — and has given the boutique a distinctive, recognizable presence in a competitive luxury market.

title: Mobile App UI Design
shortDescription: User-centered interface design for a fitness tracking application.
fullDescription: This project focused on designing the complete UI/UX for a fitness tracking mobile application targeting health-conscious users aged 18–35. The process began with user research, persona creation, and competitor analysis, followed by low-fidelity wireframes, interactive prototypes, and finally a fully detailed high-fidelity design system in Figma. The design prioritizes clarity, motivation, and ease of use — making it effortless for users to log workouts, track progress, and stay consistent with their fitness goals.
features: Onboarding flow with 4 personalized screens collecting fitness goals and experience level
Home dashboard with daily activity ring, streak counter, and quick-log shortcuts
Workout library with filter by muscle group, duration, difficulty, and equipment
Progress tracking screens with weekly and monthly chart visualizations
Custom component library with 60+ reusable UI components built in Figma
Accessible design with WCAG AA contrast compliance throughout all screens
challenges: The biggest UX challenge was designing the workout logging flow — it needed to be fast enough to use mid-workout (when the user's hands are sweaty and attention is limited) while still capturing enough data to be useful. I tested 3 different interaction patterns with real users and iterated based on their feedback until the flow was reduced to under 10 seconds per exercise log.
outcome: The final prototype was tested with 12 users and received an average System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 87, which is rated 'Excellent'. The client used the design as the direct handoff to their development team. This project deepened my expertise in mobile design patterns, micro-interactions, and the value of iterative user testing.

title: Print Campaign Design
shortDescription: Multi-channel marketing materials designed for a major product launch.
fullDescription: This project involved designing a complete suite of print and digital marketing materials for a product launch campaign. The campaign needed to work seamlessly across multiple channels — large-format outdoor banners, A4 and A5 flyers, magazine double-page spreads, social media adaptations, and point-of-sale display materials. The visual language was bold, energetic, and modern, built around a strong typographic system and a striking two-color palette that ensured maximum impact at any size.
features: Outdoor advertising designs in 6 standard billboard and banner formats
A4 and A5 double-sided flyers with bleed, trim, and safe zone properly set for print
Full-page and double-page magazine spread layouts
Point-of-sale display stand design (rollup banner and countertop display)
Social media adaptations of all materials in correct sizes for Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn
Print-ready files exported in CMYK PDF/X-1a format with correct color profiles
challenges: Managing color consistency across print and digital was the central challenge. Colors that look vibrant on screen appear significantly different when printed in CMYK. I solved this by working in CMYK from the very first design file, using physical Pantone swatches for client approval, and doing a soft-proof review at every stage before sending files to the printer.
outcome: The campaign printed and launched on schedule with zero revision requests from the printer. The client reported that the outdoor materials generated measurable foot traffic increases during the launch week. This project gave me deep practical knowledge of professional print production workflows and the technical standards required for commercial printing.

title: Web Development
shortDescription: Full-stack web application with a responsive, polished interface.
fullDescription: This project is a full-stack web application built entirely from scratch, combining a clean and responsive front-end with a structured back-end architecture. The application features user authentication, dynamic data rendering, and a fully mobile-responsive interface. Special attention was paid to both the technical architecture and the visual design — the goal was to produce something that felt as polished and professional as a commercial product, not a student project.
features: Fully responsive layout built with CSS Grid and Flexbox, tested on 6 screen sizes
Dynamic content rendering using fetch, async/await, and JSON data sources
Client-side form validation with real-time inline error messages
Smooth page transitions and scroll-triggered reveal animations
Persistent user preferences (theme, language) saved in LocalStorage
Optimized performance: lazy loading, minified assets, and efficient DOM updates
challenges: The main technical challenge was achieving smooth animations without sacrificing performance on lower-end mobile devices. I replaced scroll event listeners with the Intersection Observer API, which runs off the main thread and eliminated all jank. I also introduced will-change: transform on animated elements to hint the browser to promote them to their own GPU layer.
outcome: The application achieved a Lighthouse performance score of 94 on mobile and 98 on desktop. It became the foundation for this portfolio site and demonstrated that professional-grade web experiences can be built without any framework — just deep knowledge of HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.

title: Digital Illustrations
shortDescription: Custom artwork series created for editorial and commercial clients.
fullDescription: This series of digital illustrations was commissioned for both editorial and commercial use across a range of applications — magazine covers, article headers, product packaging, and social media campaigns. Each piece was developed through a structured creative process: brief analysis, thumbnail sketching, refined line work, color blocking, and final rendering with lighting and texture. The style balances a contemporary flat aesthetic with subtle depth and texture to create illustrations that feel both modern and warm.
features: Series of 12 original illustrations delivered in vector and raster formats
Each piece supplied in multiple file formats: AI, EPS, SVG, PNG (transparent), JPEG
Full commercial usage rights transferred to clients upon final payment
Style guide created to allow future illustrations to match the established visual language
Animated versions of 3 key illustrations created as looping GIFs for social media
All artwork supplied at 300 DPI minimum for full print compatibility
challenges: Maintaining a consistent visual style across 12 separate pieces commissioned by different clients was the primary challenge. Each client had their own specific needs and preferences, which risked fragmenting the series. I solved this by defining a strict style guide before starting any illustration — locking in line weight rules, shadow depth, color temperature, and texture intensity — and applying it uniformly across all pieces.
outcome: Three of the illustrations were featured in published magazine editions. One piece was selected for use on product packaging that entered retail distribution. This project established my illustration style as a professional service offering and directly led to two ongoing client relationships for future commissioned work.

title: Logo Collection
shortDescription: A diverse logofolio showcasing brand mark design expertise across industries.
fullDescription: This ongoing collection brings together logo and brand mark designs created for real clients and personal concept projects across a wide range of industries — including hospitality, technology, fashion, sports, food and beverage, and professional services. Each logo in the collection was designed to solve a specific brand communication problem: making a startup look credible, making a heritage brand feel modern, or making a local business stand out in a crowded market. The collection demonstrates versatility, strategic thinking, and a high standard of craft.
features: Collection of 20+ logos spanning wordmarks, lettermarks, pictorial marks, and abstract marks
Each logo delivered with full construction grid showing proportions and geometry
Dark and light background versions plus single-color and reversed variants for every logo
Client brief summary included for each real-client project explaining the strategic rationale
Logos tested and verified for scalability from favicon size (16px) to billboard scale
Full vector source files organized and archived for every logo in the collection
challenges: The ongoing challenge in logo design is achieving simplicity without losing meaning — a great logo must communicate the brand's essence instantly, work at any size, and remain distinctive in black and white before any color is applied. Each logo in this collection went through a minimum of 3 rounds of refinement before reaching this standard.
outcome: This collection has become my most powerful sales tool — it is always the first thing shown to potential clients and consistently generates trust and confidence. Several logos in the collection are now in active commercial use, appearing on storefronts, product labels, uniforms, and digital platforms. The collection continues to grow with every new project completed.
